run.final:
I submitted assessment PR-0001 for the one open failure, LH-07 at 1310-04. It puts the repair at 4 h low, 5 h likely and 7 h high, with the expected return at 14:35 on the shift clock.

- **Cause:** The suspected cause is the hydraulic pump. The crew's guess was by sound only, so it isn't confirmed.
- **Basis for the range:** The crew's radio estimate was at least 4 h. The last pump repair on LH-07 (OT-2068) took 5.0 h. LH-07 has a chronic hydraulic history, and its hydraulic inspection (OT-2110) is overdue, which is why the high end is 7 h.
- **Assumption:** I assumed the repair starts at about 09:35, when the crew reaches the site.
- **Confidence:** 0.6. The proposal lists what is missing: a confirmed diagnosis, spare pump availability and the crew's arrival time.

new_proposals.title: LH-07 hydraulic failure: repair estimate

recommendation.likely_cause: Hydraulic pump failure (suspected, not confirmed). Chronic hydraulic problem, and the PM 500 h hydraulic inspection OT-2110 is overdue.

options.scenario: low: pump fault is confirmed and a spare is on hand
likely: pump repair like OT-2068 (5.0 h)
high: the failure turns out to be a pump plus hose or seal, or parts must be fetched, or the machine must be towed (it cannot move on its own)

new_proposals.calculation: I assumed the repair starts at about 09:35, when maintenance arrives at 1310-04 (the failure was at 09:18). Crew radio estimate: at least 4 h, based on sound only, so reliability is low. CMMS history: the pump repair OT-2068 took 5.0 h, and the other hydraulic work orders took 3.5 h and 2.5 h (mean 3.67 h). Low = 4 h, the crew minimum. Likely = 5 h, the last pump repair. High = 7 h, which adds margin for the overdue PM, the chronic condition, and possible secondary hydraulic faults. Expected back = 09:35 + 5 h = 14:35. The 17:00 end of the productive window leaves little time after that.
missing_info: Diagnosis confirming the pump: ask the maintenance crew at 1310-04 once they have inspected it.
Spare hydraulic pump availability: ask the maintenance warehouse or CMMS stock.
Maintenance crew arrival time at the site, which would fix the repair start.

run.final:
I submitted proposal PR-0002 for approval. It moves LH-11 from TP-1250-02 (the lowest-grade loading-only stope, 4.1 g/t) to TP-1310-04. The move takes about 1 h, and LH-11 covers the stope until LH-07 is back, likely at 14:35.

It protects about 33.0 oz and loses about 16.0 oz at 1250-02, for a net of about 17.0 oz. Doing nothing loses about 41.1 oz. Confidence is 0.6, because the pump diagnosis and the repair time are still unconfirmed.

new_proposals.title: Reassign LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 (cover high-grade stope while LH-07 is repaired)

options.description: No reaction; TP-1310-04 (8.4 g/t) has no loader from 09:31 until LH-07 is back at 14:35 (likely case).
Hold and resume when LH-07 is repaired (likely 14:35; 13:35 low, 16:35 high). Same loss as do_nothing in the likely case; in the high case, 7.07 h x 30 = 212 t, 57.5 oz.

LH-11 from TP-1250-02 (carguio, 4.1 g/t, lowest grade; LOADER-BACKUP-01/02). Move 1 h across levels (MOVE-TIME-01), arrives 10:35 and loads until 14:35, then returns to 1250 by about 15:35. Loss at 1310-04 during the move: 30 t, 8.1 oz. Loss at 1250-02: 121.3 t, 16.0 oz. Total shown.

LH-10 from TP-1310-11 (carguio, 6.0 g/t, same level, 0.5 h move). Protects 137 t / 37.1 oz, loses 122.5 t / 23.6 oz, net 13.5 oz. Worse than LH-11 and breaks the lowest-grade rule. Total loss at 1310-04 during the move plus 1310-11 is about 145 t / 27.6 oz.

new_proposals.calculation: Oz = t x g/t / 31.1035 (the plan's formula). The loader rate at 1310-04 is 300 t / 10 h productive = 30 t/h. TP-1250-02 is 200 t / 10 h = 20 t/h. Repair back at 14:35 per PR-0001 (likely, 5 h; maintenance arrives about 09:35). Time counted from 09:31. Do nothing: 09:31 to 14:35 = 5.07 h x 30 = 152.1 t, x 8.4 / 31.1035 = 41.1 oz. Rules: LOADER-BACKUP-01 says take the loader from the lowest-grade stope. LOADER-BACKUP-02 says only phase 'carguio' stopes can give one up, so the combined-cycle stopes (DF-1310-05, TP-1220-01, TP-1280-02, TP-1310-07) are excluded. Eligible stopes: TP-1250-02 at 4.1 g/t, TP-1280-06 at 5.5, TP-1250-08 at 5.8, TP-1310-11 at 6.0, and the 1340 stopes at 6.5 or more. The lowest is TP-1250-02 (LH-11), on level 1250, so the move takes 1 h (MOVE-TIME-01), arriving about 10:35. LH-11 loads 10:35 to 14:35 = 4.07 h x 30 = 122.1 t, which is 33.0 oz protected. At 1250-02 the loss runs from 09:35 until LH-11 is back about 15:35 (6.07 h x 20 = 121.3 t x 4.1 / 31.1035 = 16.0 oz). Net = 33.0 - 16.0 = 17.0 oz. LH-11 is also the best by ounces: LH-10 nets 13.5 oz, LH-05 about 8 oz, LH-08 about 10 oz. The rule choice and the best-ounces choice agree. I kept 30 t/h for LH-11 at 1310-04; its 7 min cycle against LH-07's 6 min would make it about 26 t/h, which lowers the protected figure by about 15%. LH-07 cannot move itself and may need towing.
missing_info: The pump diagnosis is not confirmed and the repair estimate is low-reliability. Ask the maintenance crew at 1310-04 for the diagnosis.
Spare hydraulic pump stock: check the maintenance warehouse or CMMS stock.
Whether the 1250-02 face can be left safely, and the real ramp travel time for LH-11: ask the Jefe de Guardia.
If the repair runs to the high case (16:35), keep LH-11 at 1310-04 and do not return it.
